0|bc5b5b1e5111005363094da1d5f5ffb0e83165f1|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"btrfs: stop incrementing log batch when joining log transaction
When joining a log transaction we acquire the root's log mutex
increment the root's log batch and log writers counters while holding
the mutex. However we don't need to increment the log batch there
because we are holding the mutex and incremented the log writers counter
as well
column2: so any other task trying to sync log will wait for the current

column1: task to finish its logging and still achieve the desired log batching.
Since the log batch counter is an atomic counter and is incremented twice
at the very beginning of the fsync callback (btrfs_sync_file())
before flushing delalloc and once again after waiting for writeback to
complete
column2: eliminating its increment when joining the log transaction

column1: may provide some performance gains in case we have multiple concurrent
tasks doing fsyncs against different files in the same subvolume
reduces contention on the atomic (locking the cacheline and bouncing it).
When testing fio with 32 jobs
different files of the same subvolume
column2: on top of a zram device

column1: consistently see gains (higher throughput) between 1% to 2%
very low value and possibly hard to be observed with a real device (I
couldn't observe consistent gains with my low/mid end NVMe device).
So this change is mostly motivated to just simplify the logic
the log batch counter is only relevant when an fsync starts and while not
holding the root's log mutex.
